html:
Juan Vicente Gómez was the dictator of Venezuela from 1908 until his death in 1935. Under him Venezuela became the world's largest exporter of oil.

A cattle rancher from the Andes, he took power from his former ally Cipriano Castro while Castro was abroad. He built a national army and roads that ended the age of regional warlords, and paid off the foreign debt. He ruled from his ranch at Maracay and filled the jails with opponents, including the students of the Generation of 1928, among them Rómulo Betancourt.

He gave generous concessions to foreign oil companies, and after the oil strikes at Lake Maracaibo, oil money flowed to the state and to his family. When he died, he left Venezuela a centralised, oil-rich state, the base for both later democracy and Chávez.
